about: Owner-supplied and studied reference sites. Each entry is training material the builder applies automatically; owner_rules are standing feedback. Add a new reference whenever the owner sends one (utils.reference_library.add_reference).
owner_rules: No page built from stacked boxes or rows of bordered cards; sections flow into each other (applies to every page, not only the home page).
Hero patterns apply to every page: each subpage opens with its own full-bleed subject, never a plain heading in a box.
Never show the same logo twice in one view (e.g. a small nav logo next to a large hero logo); hide the nav mark while the hero mark is on screen.
Never use screenshots of websites or mock-up boxes as hero imagery; they read as cheap.
A logo animation alone is not impressive enough; impressive comes from rich real material (photo, video, lit 3D scene) and motion across the whole page.
Examples the owner sends are training data: extract the technique, add it here, and apply it to future sites without being asked.

Demos may use licensed Pexels (or other commercially licensed stock) photos, always labelled as illustrations; the final paid site is built from the client's own photos and video. Stock counts as material for a demo's level, not for the final site.

The hero subject must be the business's own world: a web studio shows websites, a renovator shows renovations. Borrowing another trade's imagery (a bathroom on a web studio) reads as the wrong company.
No grey or washed-out palettes. The site must be memorable: a confident brand colour carried through whole sections (colour fields, chapter colours), not one small accent on grey.
Choose typefaces with character for each brand; the default sans plus an italic serif is not enough on its own.

Hero order (owner, 24.11.2026): the headline and call to action are visible the moment the page opens; when the visitor starts scrolling the text moves away and the scroll animation plays; the story is short (about 1.5-2 screens) and scrolling is never blocked or slowed. This replaces the older 'copy after the final frame' choreography.

Brand continuity (owner, 24.11.2026): an existing brand is kept and made stronger, never replaced. Logo, brand colours and typeface carry through every page; a redesign may add a bolder field colour or scale, but only from the brand's own palette. Keeping a brand does not mean copying the old site: the owner rejected a redesign that stayed too close to the previous Kaurivo look. Kaurivo's new direction (24.11.2026): black and bone with Kaurivo cobalt carried as whole fields, Bricolage Grotesque display with Inter text, used identically on every page and inside every demo shown on the site.

One type system for the whole site (owner, 24.11.2026): one family is best, two at most, and illustrative content inside the site (demo pages, examples) uses the same faces. Never a new typeface per section or per example.

The first screen must say what the business does within a second, in its own world: a web studio shows a website being designed and built (layout, type, image, going live), not photos of other trades.

Showcased work keeps its own identity (owner, 24.11.2026): example or client sites shown on a studio's own site must look like different companies (own palette, typefaces, layout), never like the host site's template. The one-type-system rule covers the host site's own text; showcased work sits in a clearly framed showcase (data-showcase) with the host's caption around it.
Never ship design scaffolding as decoration: no wireframe guides, annotation labels or placeholder crosses on a finished page, and text never overlaps other text anywhere (browser QA fails it).

No shared skeleton (owner review of three demos, 24.11.2026): sites for different businesses must not repeat the same section pattern (sticky heading left + list right, giant wordmark footer). Each section's layout comes from its content: a menu reads as a menu, a calendar as a calendar, a route as a route.

Each site gets one signature interaction that belongs to its trade (e.g. dish image following the pointer over a menu, a visit calculator on a price list, a scroll story of a day at a cabin), not only fade-in reveals.

Full-bleed photography needs source images at least as wide as the largest screen it fills (about 2400 px); 1280 px stock stretched across a desktop reads as cheap and blurry. Keep one consistent light and style across a site's photos.

Hero from the library, every time (owner, 24.11.2026): every site's hero is chosen from utils.hero_library and named in the design notes; sites shown side by side (demos, a portfolio) each use a different library pattern, e.g. cinematic photo + touchable light for a restaurant, slatted reveal for a salon, giant wordmark for a cabin.

references.source: owner video 24.11.2026 (Curation by, sonic identity studio, site by Coko studio)

techniques.name: persistent atmosphere
techniques.observed: one fixed, softly lit textured background (a glowing mesh) stays behind every section while content scrolls over it
techniques.recipe: a fixed full-viewport layer (photo, video, canvas or CSS texture from the brand's material) under transparent sections; content panels never get their own boxes
techniques.needs: one atmospheric texture from the business's world

techniques.name: chapter colours
techniques.observed: each chapter tints its title and small cards with its own accent (white, purple, green) while the background stays
techniques.recipe: data-tone per section and an accent variable per chapter; type changes colour as the chapter enters
techniques.needs: 3-4 accents derived from the brand palette

techniques.name: horizontal track
techniques.observed: chapter titles and service cards slide sideways as you scroll down
techniques.recipe: data-hscroll section: sticky stage, inner track translates X with progress (utils.motion_system)

techniques.name: brand motif ending
techniques.observed: a large black-and-white photo opens under the closing call to action and a waveform motif (the brand's medium) fills the footer
techniques.recipe: closing section with one full-bleed photo revealed by mask and a motif drawn from the business's own medium
techniques.needs: one strong closing image; a motif that belongs to the trade

techniques.name: tone blend
techniques.observed: page background blends white -> warm brown -> black between sections
techniques.recipe: data-tone=#hex on sections (utils.motion_system)

techniques.name: depth wall
techniques.observed: a 3D wall of real sites the camera flies through
techniques.recipe: data-depth-wall with data-col children

techniques.name: live product demo
techniques.observed: the product types a business name live as the section enters
techniques.recipe: a small real interaction of the business's own tool or booking flow

techniques.name: transition as scroll
techniques.observed: full-bleed scene flows into the next (through clouds)
techniques.recipe: stacked full-bleed scenes with scroll-linked scale/opacity crossfade

techniques.name: live 3D room
techniques.observed: a real-estate hero moves from room to room
techniques.recipe: sequence of interior photos or a 3D scene, one room per scroll step

techniques.name: spatial browsing
techniques.observed: products float in space and glide past
techniques.recipe: data-depth-wall with product cut-outs

techniques.name: touchable surface
techniques.observed: a portrait ripples under the cursor
techniques.recipe: cursor light or displacement on the hero image, paired with another pattern

references.source: Awwwards Sites of the Month, studied 24.11.2026

techniques.name: giant wordmark
techniques.observed: THE LINE, Watson, Akaru: the name across the full width, cropped by the edge
techniques.recipe: HERO_LIBRARY 2

techniques.name: cinematic photo
techniques.observed: Son Daven, Terminal: one full-bleed image, lots of quiet space
techniques.recipe: HERO_LIBRARY 1

techniques.name: slatted reveal
techniques.observed: Siena: the name seen through moving vertical slats
techniques.recipe: HERO_LIBRARY 7

techniques.name: video + index
techniques.observed: Inkfish: full-bleed footage with a quiet project list
techniques.recipe: HERO_LIBRARY 8

techniques.name: scattered gallery
techniques.observed: Floema: product photos scattered on a calm canvas
techniques.recipe: HERO_LIBRARY 6

references.source: owner link 24.11.2026 (landonorris.com, Awwwards Site of the Year level)

techniques.name: 3D portrait hero
techniques.observed: a lit 3D head scan wears the helmet that turns with the cursor over a pale topographic line background
techniques.recipe: one real 3D/photographic subject of the person or product that answers the cursor; a quiet line motif from the brand's world behind it
techniques.needs: a 3D scan, product model or cut-out photo of the real subject

techniques.name: signature stroke
techniques.observed: a neon handwritten signature draws itself over a black-and-white portrait as it scrolls in
techniques.recipe: inline SVG path of the owner's signature or a brand mark, stroke-dashoffset driven by scroll progress over a duotone photo
techniques.needs: a signature or mark as SVG; one portrait or work photo

techniques.name: mixed-type manifesto
techniques.observed: a giant statement in two faces (italic serif accent words in neon, condensed caps in bone) fills and overflows the screen and brightens word by word while scrolling
techniques.recipe: one manifesto paragraph set at 9-12vw, words wrapped in spans whose opacity/colour follow scroll progress; accent words in a second typeface
techniques.needs: one true sentence about the business

techniques.name: giant marquee
techniques.observed: huge words slide sideways across the section edge
techniques.recipe: kinetic type band (utils.kinetic_type) at display size, scroll-linked direction

techniques.name: captioned photo collage
techniques.observed: photos at different sizes scroll at different speeds, each with a small place-and-year caption
techniques.recipe: absolute-positioned real photos with per-image parallax speed and a tiny caption; no frames or cards

techniques.name: split giant links
techniques.observed: ON TRACK / OFF TRACK as two huge words that act as the navigation into two worlds
techniques.recipe: two full-width typographic links with hover image reveal instead of cards
techniques.needs: two clear paths through the site

techniques.name: object carousel
techniques.observed: a hall of fame of helmets as a horizontal sequence of rotating objects with year labels
techniques.recipe: data-hscroll track of cut-out product images, each turning slightly with progress
techniques.needs: cut-out photos of the business's signature objects

techniques.name: tight brand palette
techniques.observed: dark olive, bone and one neon lime used everywhere, including the cursor and strokes
techniques.recipe: one dark ground, one light ink and one loud accent reserved for strokes and emphasis words

techniques.name: measured brand system
techniques.observed: Firecrawl branding scan: dark olive ground #282C20, bone text #F4F4ED, one acid accent #D2FF00 used for links and the primary button only; display face Brier (characterful) over Mona Sans body; 1px radii, 9.6px button radius, no shadows
techniques.recipe: tinted dark ground taken from the subject's world (not neutral black), warm off-white text, exactly one loud accent reserved for actions; one display face with character plus a plain sans; near-square corners and no shadows
techniques.needs: nothing beyond a chosen accent and display face

references.source: owner video 24.11.2026 (Adrien Ninet, 'make your web design look 10x better': fonts shown on real sites)

techniques.name: Fraunces editorial
techniques.observed: a warm soft serif set large and light, with small images and emoji placed inside the sentence
techniques.recipe: Fraunces (Google Fonts) 300-400 for big statements; inline rounded photos between words for personal or crafted brands
techniques.needs: a personal, warm or crafted brand

techniques.name: Montserrat bold product
techniques.observed: heavy geometric sans on a saturated blue field for a confident product claim
techniques.recipe: Montserrat 800 headlines on a full colour field; plain body

techniques.name: Inter quiet portfolio
techniques.observed: Inter at large size with two greys for a calm professional introduction
techniques.recipe: Inter / Inter Display, size contrast instead of weight contrast

techniques.name: Sora big word
techniques.observed: one oversized word ('botanical') over a full-bleed photo
techniques.recipe: Sora 600-700 at 15-20vw for a single word over imagery
techniques.needs: one strong photo and one word that sums up the business

techniques.name: Space Grotesk giant crop
techniques.observed: a name in Space Grotesk so large it is cropped by the viewport
techniques.recipe: Space Grotesk 500-700 at 25vw+, cropped; pairs with the giant-wordmark hero

techniques.name: Inter Tight on glow
techniques.observed: tight display type on black with a soft colour glow behind
techniques.recipe: Inter Tight 500 with -0.04em tracking over a blurred gradient blob

techniques.name: Satoshi + italic serif
techniques.observed: clean grotesk with one italic serif phrase ('one task at a time') over a vivid gradient product shot
techniques.recipe: Satoshi (Fontshare, free licence) or Instrument Sans with Instrument Serif italic for the accent phrase

techniques.name: choose fonts per brand
techniques.observed: the same layout looks ten times better with the right typeface
techniques.recipe: pick one display face from this list by the brand's character and keep the body face plain; never default to the same font for every site
